title: SOULFLY Fires Bassist Mike Leon
text:
Soulfly fans, major news! The iconic metal band has announced bassist Mike Leon ‘s departure, sparking anticipation for their future sound. learn about this shift and get the inside scoop on Max Cavalera’s plans to bring the band back to its tribal roots for their next album,promising a powerful experience for listeners eager to experience the new Soulfly lineup and music.
Soulfly Announces Bassist Departure,Plans for Future Tribal Sound Published: April 10,2024
By [Your Name/Organization]
After a long tenure,Soulfly and bassist Mike Leon have parted ways. Max Cavalera hints at a return to the band’s tribal roots for their next album.
Soulfly. Image for illustrative purposes only. Bassist Mike Leon Exits Soulfly Soulfly, the influential metal band fronted by Max Cavalera, has announced the departure of bassist Mike Leon. Leon, who previously played with Havok , joined Soulfly in September 2015. He stepped in following the exit of Static-X bassist Tony Campos earlier that year. The band confirmed the news via social media.
The band released a statement, saying: After many strong years together, SOULFLY is parting ways with bassist Mike Leon. The tribe are still performing at the upcoming Mexico City’s Nu Metal Revolution on may 3rd with the Sorcerer, Igor Amadeus , of CAVALERA band, GO AHEAD AND DIE and HEALING MAGIC filling in.
The statement continued, we’re going in different directions now and we thank Mike for all the time spent with us rocking hard on stage!
Igor Amadeus Cavalera , son of Max Cavalera, will fill in on bass for the upcoming “Nu Metal Revolution” performance in Mexico City.
Touring Continues in Support of “Totem” Despite the lineup change, Soulfly is continuing its tour in support of their latest album, “Totem” , released in August 2022 through Nuclear Blast . “Totem” is the follow-up to 2018’s “Ritual” . The album was recorded at Platinum Underground in Mesa, Arizona. John Aquilino and Arthur Rizk handled recording duties, with assistance from John Powers.
Produced by max Cavalera and Arthur Rizk. Features guest appearances from John Powers (Eternal Champion), Chris Ulsh (Power Trip), and John Tardy (Obituary). Arthur Rizk also played lead guitar on the album. Artwork created by James Bousema. The album showcases Soulfly’s signature blend of heavy metal and tribal influences, a sound that Cavalera is keen to revisit in future releases.
Max Cavalera on Soulfly’s Future Direction In a November 2024 interview, Max Cavalera discussed the direction of the next Soulfly album, tentatively slated for a late 2025 release. he emphasized a return to the band’s core sound.
[It will be] very tribal, back to basics. I’m gonna let SOULFLY be SOULFLY again. I kind of stopped SOULFLY from being SOULFLY for a couple of years, and I kind of regret that a little bit. But now that I have CAVALERA and GO AHEAD AND DIE and KILLER BE KILLED , I get to really let SOULFLY be SOULFLY . Let’s go back to what it was in the beginning. it’s that tribal groove power that people love. So I’m creating a record with that.
Max Cavalera, Metal-Roos Interview
Cavalera’s comments suggest a renewed focus on the elements that defined Soulfly’s early work, promising a powerful and groove-laden experience for fans.
Cavalera’s enduring Passion for Metal At 55, Max Cavalera shows no signs of slowing down. He reaffirmed his dedication to music and performing.
I was put on this planet to do this, and that’s all I wanna do. It’s all I know how to do and it’s all I wanna do… Of course, we change as people as we get older, but I think there’s some things in me, they are the same as they were when I was 15 years old — my passion for metal, how I feel about going on the stage and the goosebumps, the excitement is like a drug.You can’t really get that anywhere else except on the stage. And those things don’t change. And I love that.
Max Cavalera, Metal-Roos Interview
Cavalera’s enthusiasm for metal remains undiminished, driving his continued creativity and performance energy.
to me, I’m always looking forward to whatever tour we’re doing, whatever album we’re making. There are challenges, but at the same time, they are great life opportunities. And I live life for the moment. I’m not one of those guys that — I don’t live thinking 10 years from now. I live for right now for this, ’cause I don’t know what’s 10 years from now. I live the moment, and in the moment, this is what’s going on right now. I grab it with both hands,man,and enjoy. And I try to teach that to my kids — enjoy the moment. It’s a great thing. It’s good to be alive. It’s good to share this feeling with people around you. It’s incredible. It’s an incredible thing.
Max cavalera, Metal-Roos Interview
His beliefs of living in the moment and embracing opportunities continues to fuel his career and inspire those around him.
Past Lineup Shifts This isn’t the first lineup change for soulfly in recent years.In August 2021, the band parted ways with longtime guitarist Marc Rizzo due to personal differences.Fear Factory’s Dino Cazares filled in on guitar for Soulfly’s 2021 and 2022 shows.
Guitarist Mike DeLeon has been touring with Soulfly for two years. Before joining Soulfly, DeLeon was a member of Pantera singer Philip Anselmo’s solo band, Philip H. Anselmo & The Illegals. he replaced Marzi Montazeri in 2015. DeLeon also filled in for Zakk Wylde at the first rehearsal for the fall 2022 Pantera shows, showcasing his versatility and talent within the metal community.
